question.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$

current_example.problem: Given that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14168227/assets/08a2e3f949362198fd320b83fbfdd4ad4a3996aa63ca25264a0ab9b1c720f8e6.svg) express the quadratic form $Q(\mathbf{x})= x_1x_2+2x_2^2$ in terms of the components of $\mathbf{y}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14168227/assets/41fce2ec05aadd02fc793da57280f93165a43ce774de184ee70a6687d73e3e74.svg) 

gives the following expressions for $y_1$ and $y_2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & =-{x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the second equation for $x_1$ and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for $x_1$ and $x_2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =-{y}_{1}-2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(-{y}_{2})(-{y}_{1}-2{y}_{2})+2(-{y}_{1}-2{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}^{2}+2{y}_{1}^{2}+8{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+8{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2{y}_{1}^{2}+9{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+10{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
